items.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had used him on some of my records, Horace, Kenny Clarke and Percy Heath.

ctx.x: Doug Watkins, yeah, from Detroit. They didn’t last. It was supposed to be co-op, but it turned out not to be co-op [laughs], so Horace got his own group and had me in the group. Me and Hank Mobley was in the group. We played around quite a bit. We never went out west, but we played Chicago, Pittsburgh, Philadelphia, and Washington, all the places around this part of the world. Horace was a fine guy. I had recorded with Horace. I had used him on some of my records, Horace, Kenny Clarke and Percy Heath. That’s one…

items.title: Percy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: there are so many records you made on the Prestige and Blue Note labels with people like Art Farmer

ctx.x: Yeah, maybe it was Gilly. But the Symphony Sid All-Stars, and oh yeah, JJ Johnson was in that too. We played around there in the Downbeat with that group. The two clubs were interrelated anyhow. Being in New York then working sometimes with Miles, made these record dates with Miles and everybody else who recorded for Prestige at that time, Thad Jones, you mentioned Art Farmer, who had left the Jazztet, he and Benny had when Tootie was playing with them incidentally. You remember the Jazztet?
Wasn’t the Jazztet later? I thought the Jazztet was formed like in 1959. But there was a Jazztet…
